message.content:
Here’s a quick roundup of some of the most highly regarded crime‑thriller films released in 2020 (and early 2021, as many were delayed):

| Film | Director | Key Cast | Why It Stands Out |
|------|----------|----------|-------------------|
| **The Invisible Man** (2020) | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | A fresh take on the classic horror‑thriller hybrid, blending psychological suspense with social commentary on domestic abuse. |
| **The Trial of the Chicago 7** (2020) | Aaron Sorkin | Eddie Redmayne, Sacha Baron Cohen, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II | A courtroom drama that doubles as a tense political thriller, capturing the chaos of the 1969 protest trial. |
| **The Hunt** (2020) | Thomas Vinterberg | Mads Mikkelsen, Nikolaj Coster-Waldau | A chilling moral thriller about a group of men who orchestrate a hunt for a young boy, exploring themes of paranoia and mob mentality. |
| **The Gentlemen** (2020) | Guy Ritchie | Matthew McConaughey, Charlie Hunnam, Hugh Grant | Ritchie's signature fast‑paced, witty crime caper featuring a complex web of betrayals and double-crosses. |
| **The Irishman** (2020) | Martin Scorsese | Robert De Niro, Al Pacino, Joe Pesci | Though more of a crime epic, its slow‑burn narrative and masterful storytelling make it a standout thriller. |
| **The Night House** (2020) | David Bruckner | Rebecca Hall, Nathan Lane | A psychological thriller that blends supernatural elements with a haunting exploration of grief and trauma. |
| **The Last Duel** (2020) | Ridley Scott | Matt Damon, Adam Driver, Jodie Comer | A historical crime drama that turns into a tense duel of honor and betrayal, with a strong focus on character dynamics. |
| **The Platform** (2020) | Galder Gaztelu-Urrutia | Iván Massagué, Zorion Eguileor | A dystopian thriller that uses a vertical prison setting to explore class warfare and human desperation. |
| **The Invisible Man** (2020) | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | A modern twist on the classic horror‑thriller, blending psychological suspense with social commentary on domestic abuse. |
| **The Hunt** (2020) | Thomas Vinterberg | Mads Mikkelsen, Nikolaj Coster-Waldau | A chilling moral thriller about a group of men who orchestrate a hunt for a young boy, exploring themes of paranoia and mob mentality. |

These films cover a range of sub‑genres—from psychological thrillers to courtroom dramas—while maintaining the core tension and intrigue that define crime‑thrillers. Enjoy!
